Yes. A **13.5-hectare tree-cover loss candidate** was detected on the property in 2025, covering about 3.9% of its area. The 2020 forest reference agrees with 98% of the candidate area.

The finding is **pending corroboration** because 2025 is the latest year observed; a later year is needed to assess persistence. It does not establish deforestation, the cause of the loss, or whether it was legal.
